森林齊特琴源自德國，屬西特恩琴一類，以撥弦發聲。二十世紀上半葉，製造者曾試圖把它: The waldzither comes from Germany, a plucked instrument of the cittern type. In the first half of the twentieth century makers tried to establish it as the German national instrument, at a time when more complex instruments were hard to obtain and hard to afford. It has nine or ten steel strings in five courses, usually in open C tuning; the fifth string is two octaves below the banjolin. It is one of the few instruments still using Preston pegs, the other being the Portuguese guitar. Without the lowest single course it is sometimes called a waldoline, a name made from waldzither and mandolin; folklore has it that Martin Luther played a cittern-like instrument at the Wartburg.

The waldzither is a plucked instrument from Germany, of the cittern family, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.322. It usually has nine or ten steel strings in five courses and is mostly tuned open; open C tuning is the most common. It uses Preston pegs and sounds by plucking. In the first half of the twentieth century, when more complex instruments were hard to obtain and hard to afford, makers tried to establish it as a German national instrument.
